evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))

evaluated.name: Persistent Book-Over-Cash Margin Drift
evaluated.expression: RANK(WINSOR(MA(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, DELTA(wcap, 1)), sale), 1)), 3), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms should earn lower subsequent returns when reported gross-margin changes persistently exceed changes in working-capital-neutral operating cash margins.
evaluated.reasoning: Adding the working-capital change back to operating cash flow removes short-term cash-conversion timing before comparing it with reported margin dynamics. Unlike an absolute alignment score or a dual-improvement bottleneck, this signed signal isolates the economically suspicious direction in which book performance repeatedly outruns core cash performance.

evaluated.name: Depreciation-Conservative Margin Gains
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3)), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))

evaluated.name: Accrual-Light Margin Inflection
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(ABS(ACCEL(RATIO(wcap, sale))))), INDICATOR(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), 0))

evaluated.reasoning: Margin acceleration identifies an early operating recovery rather than another current-level margin-improvement screen. evaluated.name: Growth-Confirmed Asset-Release Funding
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(NEG(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1))), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale)), MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0), INDICATOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 0)))

evaluated.reasoning: The prior negative long-short alpha may reflect extreme asset releases by shrinking firms whose margins improved through retrenchment rather than durable operations. Requiring actual sales growth removes that liquidation channel and tests asset-side cash realization only when the underlying business is expanding.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Contraction-Confirmed Working-Capital Squeeze
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))))), MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0), INDICATOR(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)), 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: When both sales and gross margins are declining, simultaneous noncash current-asset accumulation and current-liability growth should predict lower subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Working-capital buildup during margin decline can represent productive expansion when sales are still growing, potentially explaining the earlier positive-slope but negative-alpha conflict. evaluated.name: Smooth-Earnings Cash-to-Accrual Substitution
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)))))), INDICATOR(NEG(ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))), 0))

evaluated.name: Smooth-Earnings Noncash-Asset Share Drift
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), act), 1))), INDICATOR(NEG(ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))), 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms with smooth earnings, growth in the noncash share of current assets should predict lower subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This stock-composition formulation measures whether current assets are shifting away from cash toward receivables, inventory, and other accrual assets, rather than relying on the conjunction of two flow changes. evaluated.name: Smooth-Earnings Accrual Lock-In
evaluated.expression: RANK(NEG(MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), act), 5), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))))))

evaluated.name: Margin-Cash Composition Volatility Wedge
evaluated.expression: RANK(NEG(MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(che, act), 5)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))))

evaluated.reasoning: The signal tests a volatility wedge rather than smoothing the original substitution flows through time. evaluated.name: Margin-Gain Liquid-Asset Confirmation
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when gross-margin improvement is accompanied by an increasing cash share of current assets.

evaluated.name: Persistent Profit Liquidity Floor

considered.name: Clean Working-Capital Margin
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))

considered.name: Cash-Book Stability Bottleneck
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 3))), RANK(NEG(MAX(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), ABS(SUB(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when accrual burdens are low and stable reported earnings are corroborated by similarly stable cash flows.

considered.name: Accrual-Enabled Smoothing Penalty
considered.expression: NEG(MIN(RANK(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 3)), RANK(SUB(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when a high recurring accrual burden coincides with operating cash flows that are substantially more volatile than reported earnings.
considered.reasoning: The directional volatility wedge identifies cases in which accruals may be smoothing volatile cash performance rather than simply rewarding low earnings volatility. The minimum creates a high-high conjunction: the penalty becomes severe only when both accrual reliance and the cash-versus-book smoothing wedge are elevated, limiting contamination from either standalone anomaly.

considered.name: Neutralized Persistent-Profit Accrual Screen
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 3))), INDICATOR(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ib, at), 0), 5), 3))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms profitable in at least four of the past five periods, lower recurring accrual intensity should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Industry-standardizing the accrual score produces positive and negative values, so firms failing the profitability screen receive a neutral score of zero instead of being forced into the short leg. considered.name: Profit Cash-Backing Persistence

considered.reasoning: Each profitable period contributes positively when cash flow confirms the profit and negatively when the reported profit lacks even directional cash backing; unprofitable periods contribute zero. This categorical persistence mechanism is distinct from the continuous Sloan accrual spread and directly targets repeated paper-profit episodes without assigning all nonprofitable firms to an extreme portfolio leg.

considered.name: Demand-Accrual Volatility Alignment
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MAX(RANK(VOL(RATIO(revt, at), 3)), RANK(SUB(VOL(RATIO(ADD(ABS(recch), ABS(invch)), at), 3), VOL(RATIO(revt, at), 3))))))

considered.reasoning: The first channel penalizes unstable revenue productivity, while the second isolates excess volatility in receivable and inventory adjustments relative to revenue volatility. considered.name: Retained Earnings Accrual Efficiency

considered.name: Leveraged Opaque-Accrual Penalty
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ABS(txach), ABS(aoloch)), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))

considered.name: Smooth-Earnings Accrual Spike
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MIN(RANK(TS_RANK(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should underperform when working-capital accruals spike relative to their own history while reported earnings remain unusually smooth.
considered.reasoning: The temporal rank identifies an accrual spike rather than rewarding a persistently low average accrual level, while the second channel identifies smooth earnings. considered.name: Realized Retained Earnings
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 5), MAX(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 5))), 1)))

considered.reasoning: The signal penalizes retained earnings growth that outruns both cash realization and real-side operating progress, which is more suggestive of accounting accumulation than productive reinvestment. considered.name: Receivable-Revenue Acceleration Match
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(WINSOR(ABS(SUB(ACCEL(RATIO(NEG(recch), at)), ACCEL(RATIO(sale, at)))), 1)))

considered.reasoning: Negated recch approximates receivable investment, so a mismatch with sales acceleration can reveal channel stuffing, premature revenue recognition, or deteriorating collection quality. considered.name: Retained Earnings Clean-Build Bottleneck
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher returns when retained earnings accumulate persistently without recurring working-capital accrual investment.
considered.reasoning: The minimum approximates a conjunctive double sort, requiring both retained earnings growth and clean working-capital conversion. considered.name: Debt-Adjusted Cash Retention
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 5)), RANK(SUB(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Persistent retained earnings should predict higher returns when accompanied by cash accumulation that is not financed by increasing debt.
considered.reasoning: Retained earnings provide the reported-performance channel, while debt-adjusted cash growth tests whether that performance is realized as internally generated liquidity. considered.expression: RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, recch), at), 3), VOL(RATIO(ADD(ni, recch), at), 3)))

considered.reasoning: Under the cash-flow-statement convention, recch offsets the receivable component embedded in net income, so ADD(ni, recch) approximates earnings after receivable cash conversion. considered.name: Opaque Accrual Reversal Load

considered.name: Margin Improvement Funding Test
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, those requiring less noncash working-capital investment should earn higher subsequent returns.

considered.hypothesis: Among firms with stable demand, lower volatility in receivable and inventory accrual activity should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The demand-volatility indicator defines the economic subset, and the centered accrual-volatility score orders firms only within that condition. This avoids subtracting incomparable raw volatilities, prevents revenue volatility from dominating the signal, and directly tests whether stable demand is accompanied by stable operating accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Decline Working-Capital Dislocation
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(ABS(ACCEL(RATIO(wcap, sale))))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with deteriorating gross margins, lower acceleration in working-capital intensity should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Margin deterioration is especially concerning when accompanied by a sharp change of change in working-capital needs, which can indicate inventory, collection, or payment-policy disruption. Using absolute acceleration avoids treating distress-driven working-capital liquidation as favorable and tests instability rather than the published accrual level.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Depreciation-Supported Margin Improvement
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Gross-margin improvement should predict higher returns when it is not accompanied by a declining depreciation charge relative to sales.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the expansion gate with a ranked margin-change channel removes the growth exposure that may have produced a strong Fama-MacBeth slope but weak FF5 alpha. The second channel tests conservative expense recognition: apparent margin gains are less credible when depreciation intensity is simultaneously being reduced.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Verified Working-Capital Harvest
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale))))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, prior working-capital investment should be favorable only when it reverses into a current working-capital release.
considered.reasoning: The minimum explicitly requires both a prior-period buildup and a current-period release, rather than rewarding the lagged accrual magnitude additively. Centering the verified reversal score before applying the margin gate keeps other firms neutral and distinguishes temporary investment realization from persistent high accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self-Funded Trade Margin Gains
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(RATIO(recch, sale)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(apalch, sale))))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, simultaneous receivable collection and limited reliance on payable growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Positive recch indicates customer cash realization, while positive apalch supplies cash through increased supplier financing; the latter is therefore treated as a funding dependency rather than mislabeled as a cash cost. Rank normalization makes the two trade-credit channels commensurable, and the minimum requires both customer collection and supplier independence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dual Margin Cash Confirmation
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, apalch), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when gross margins and supplier-neutral operating cash margins improve together.
considered.reasoning: One channel measures improvement in reported operating economics, while the other measures improvement in cash generation after removing support from payable accruals. The conjunctive rank structure tests simultaneous book-and-cash confirmation rather than combining a profitability floor with another standalone cash-flow trend.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Smooth-Earnings Supplier-Funded Inventory
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(NEG(invch), cogs)), RANK(RATIO(apalch, cogs))))), INDICATOR(NEG(ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with smooth earnings, inventory buildup financed by increasing accounts payable should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Negated invch captures inventory investment, while positive apalch captures supplier financing; their high-high conjunction identifies inventory accumulation whose cash burden is hidden by stretched payment terms. The centered negative penalty orders firms within the smooth-earnings condition and replaces another demand-volatility variant with a distinct financing-of-accruals mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Two-Sided Margin Accounting Confirmation
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3)))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, low working-capital investment and nondeclining depreciation intensity should jointly predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Working-capital investment tests whether the margin gain consumes cash, while the depreciation channel tests whether the gain is being created by reducing expense recognition. Requiring both confirmations combines the strongest portfolio-performing margin-funding mechanism with the depreciation channel’s cross-sectional strength.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Efficient Depreciation Congruence
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(ABS(SUB(GROWTH(dpc, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1))), 3), 1))), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))))), INDICATOR(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among expanding firms, depreciation growth congruence should predict higher returns when expansion also requires little noncash working-capital accrual.
considered.reasoning: Depreciation congruence alone generated strong Fama-MacBeth evidence but weak long-short alpha, consistent with its extremes retaining generic expansion exposure. The added working-capital bottleneck requires expansion to be both accounting-consistent and cash-efficient, which should improve abnormal-return separation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Quiet-Margin Working-Capital Dislocation
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MUL(RANK(ABS(ACCEL(RATIO(wcap, sale)))), RANK(NEG(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)))))))
considered.hypothesis: Large working-capital dislocations should predict lower returns when reported gross margins change very little.
considered.reasoning: The first channel identifies sharp changes in working-capital intensity, while the second is large only when margins appear unusually quiet. Their high-high interaction targets hidden balance-sheet instability behind smooth reported performance without combining separately normalized margin regimes or loading mechanically on a margin-direction dummy.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Decline Depreciation Stability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(ABS(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3)))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with declining gross margins, a stable depreciation charge relative to sales should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Operating deterioration creates incentives to alter depreciation assumptions to soften reported weakness, so instability in depreciation intensity is more informative in this state. This replaces the leverage overlay with a directly attributable expense-recognition mechanism and does not reward either sharp depreciation cuts or distress-driven increases.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent-Profit Trade-Credit Trap
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(apalch, sale), 3)), RANK(MA(RATIO(NEG(recch), sale), 3))))), INDICATOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ni, at), 3), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among persistently profitable firms, simultaneous receivable buildup and reliance on increasing payables should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Payable growth supplies cash, but when it persistently finances receivable growth it indicates that reported profits remain trapped in customer credit and require supplier support. The high-high penalty has an ex-ante cash-cycle interpretation and does not reward gross trade-credit churn based on a prior backtest sign reversal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Depreciation-Stripped Nonworking Accrual Quality
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(ni, oancf), dpc), DELTA(wcap, 1)), at)), 3))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, lower nonworking accrual residuals after explicitly removing depreciation should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Adding dpc back to the total-accrual measure removes the mechanical depreciation component before subtracting working-capital accruals, leaving a cleaner residual of other noncash adjustments. The margin-improvement condition tests whether favorable operating news is supported without opaque nonworking accruals rather than inadvertently sorting on capital intensity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Down Dual Accounting Stability
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(ABS(ACCEL(RATIO(wcap, sale)))), NEG(ABS(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3))))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with declining gross margins, stability in both working-capital intensity and depreciation policy should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Working-capital acceleration captures balance-sheet dislocation, while depreciation-intensity drift captures expense-recognition instability during operating stress. Combining the two directly extends the separately positive margin-decline mechanisms without introducing a generic leverage characteristic.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Core-Cash Margin Co-Stability
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MAX(RANK(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3)), RANK(VOL(RATIO(ADD(oancf, DELTA(wcap, 1)), sale), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when both reported gross margins and working-capital-neutral operating cash margins are stable.
considered.reasoning: Adding the working-capital change back to operating cash flow removes short-term cash-conversion timing and approximates the underlying operating cash margin. The maximum imposes a weakest-link test, so smooth book margins do not qualify when core cash economics remain unstable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working-Capital-Neutral Margin Alignment
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(ABS(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, DELTA(wcap, 1)), sale), 1))), 3), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when changes in reported gross margins remain aligned with changes in working-capital-neutral operating cash margins.
considered.reasoning: The signal compares two commensurately scaled margin changes after removing working-capital timing from the cash-flow channel. Persistent disagreement identifies reported operating improvements or declines that are not corroborated by underlying cash economics.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Asset-Release Margin Funding Quality
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(NEG(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1))), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale)), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, cash conversion driven by noncash current-asset release rather than nondebt current-liability growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: A low net working-capital accrual can arise either from collecting or liquidating noncash current assets, or from stretching suppliers and other current creditors. The expression separates those sources, rewarding asset-side realization and liability paydown while penalizing creditor-funded margin improvement.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Decline Working-Capital Squeeze
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with declining gross margins, simultaneous noncash current-asset accumulation and nondebt current-liability growth should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The high-high conjunction identifies firms whose deteriorating operations both trap resources in noncash current assets and increasingly rely on current creditors for financing. This source-specific squeeze mechanism differs from sorting on the level or volatility of aggregate working-capital accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent Book-Over-Cash Margin Drift
considered.expression: RANK(WINSOR(MA(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, DELTA(wcap, 1)), sale), 1)), 3), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn lower subsequent returns when reported gross-margin changes persistently exceed changes in working-capital-neutral operating cash margins.
considered.reasoning: Adding the working-capital change back to operating cash flow removes short-term cash-conversion timing before comparing it with reported margin dynamics. Unlike an absolute alignment score or a dual-improvement bottleneck, this signed signal isolates the economically suspicious direction in which book performance repeatedly outruns core cash performance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Depreciation-Conservative Margin Gains
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(dpc, sale), 3)), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, nondeclining depreciation intensity should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This isolates the directional expense-recognition mechanism that produced aligned evidence in the earlier depreciation-supported margin signal. Margin gains are more credible when they are not accompanied by a reduction in depreciation charges relative to operating scale.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual-Light Margin Inflection
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(ABS(ACCEL(RATIO(wcap, sale))))), INDICATOR(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Positive margin inflections should predict higher returns when they occur without a sharp acceleration or liquidation in working-capital intensity.
considered.reasoning: Margin acceleration identifies an early operating recovery rather than another current-level margin-improvement screen. Low absolute working-capital acceleration distinguishes a genuine operating inflection from one created by aggressive balance-sheet investment or distress-driven liquidation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Creditor-Independent Durable Margins
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))), INDICATOR(ZSCORE(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with above-average durable gross margins, lower growth in nondebt current liabilities should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The quality condition selects firms whose margin level is high relative to its own instability, while the accrual channel tests whether that durability depends on stretching suppliers and other current creditors. Isolating the liability side distinguishes creditor-independent cash quality from the aggregate working-capital magnitude used by the original winner.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Growth-Confirmed Asset-Release Funding
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(NEG(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1))), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale)), MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0), INDICATOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 0)))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with both margin improvement and sales growth, current-asset realization with limited reliance on current-liability growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The prior negative long-short alpha may reflect extreme asset releases by shrinking firms whose margins improved through retrenchment rather than durable operations. Requiring actual sales growth removes that liquidation channel and tests asset-side cash realization only when the underlying business is expanding.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Contraction-Confirmed Working-Capital Squeeze
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))))), MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0), INDICATOR(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)), 0)))
considered.hypothesis: When both sales and gross margins are declining, simultaneous noncash current-asset accumulation and current-liability growth should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Working-capital buildup during margin decline can represent productive expansion when sales are still growing, potentially explaining the earlier positive-slope but negative-alpha conflict. Restricting the squeeze mechanism to actual sales contraction isolates firms trapping cash in current assets while increasingly relying on creditors despite shrinking operations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Smooth-Earnings Cash-to-Accrual Substitution
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)))))), INDICATOR(NEG(ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with smooth earnings, simultaneous cash depletion and accumulation of noncash current assets should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The high-high conjunction identifies a balance-sheet substitution in which liquid cash is replaced by receivables, inventory, or other noncash current assets while reported income remains unusually stable. This is a distinct cash-composition mechanism rather than another depreciation-policy signal or aggregate working-capital accrual sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Smooth-Earnings Noncash-Asset Share Drift
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), act), 1))), INDICATOR(NEG(ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms with smooth earnings, growth in the noncash share of current assets should predict lower subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This stock-composition formulation measures whether current assets are shifting away from cash toward receivables, inventory, and other accrual assets, rather than relying on the conjunction of two flow changes. It provides a broader-coverage test of the same economic mechanism while producing a continuous ordering that may strengthen cross-sectional evidence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Smooth-Earnings Accrual Lock-In
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), act), 5), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, at), 3))))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn lower subsequent returns when smooth earnings coincide with a noncash current-asset share near the top of the firm’s own historical range.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the extra profitability filter with a continuous interaction between earnings smoothness and an accrual-balance-sheet state. A persistently elevated noncash asset share indicates accrual lock-in rather than a one-period cash-to-accrual flow, while firms with volatile earnings do not receive the same penalty.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Cash Composition Volatility Wedge
considered.expression: RANK(NEG(MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(che, act), 5)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn lower subsequent returns when stable gross margins coexist with a volatile cash share of current assets.
considered.reasoning: The signal tests a volatility wedge rather than smoothing the original substitution flows through time. Large liquidity-composition fluctuations behind smooth operating margins suggest that balance-sheet timing or reclassification, rather than stable cash economics, is supporting reported performance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Durable-Margin Cash-Share Floor
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), TS_RANK(RATIO(che, act), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Durable gross margins should predict higher returns when the firm’s cash share of current assets is also high relative to its own history.
considered.reasoning: The cash-share state is continuous, so the construction does not discard information through a hard margin-quality gate. The bottleneck requires both persistent operating economics and historically strong liquidity composition, replacing the prior flow-substitution screen with a stock-based corroboration mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Gain Liquid-Asset Confirmation
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when gross-margin improvement is accompanied by an increasing cash share of current assets.
considered.reasoning: Both channels are continuous, similarly scaled changes, avoiding another binary gate applied to the archived substitution score. A rising cash share provides balance-sheet confirmation that the margin gain is improving liquidity composition rather than being absorbed by receivables, inventory, or other current accrual assets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent Profit Liquidity Floor
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ni, at), 3)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(che, act), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when both profitability and the cash share of current assets remain strong even in their weakest recent periods.
considered.reasoning: The dual downside floor focuses on durable cash-backed quality rather than blending two signals that share the same current-asset-change term. It requires persistent reported earnings and persistent liquidity simultaneously, reducing sensitivity to one-period accrual movements or temporary cash spikes.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the product of two canonical published anomalies — accrual quality/|accruals| (Sloan; Francis et al.) and stable ROA profitability (Novy-Marx; earnings-volatility literature) — combined by the most generic possible operator (rank multiplication), so it adds little beyond a standard quality composite and its interaction is not identified against the two additive main effects.

The gate is mis-constructed for the stated hypothesis: multiplying a non-negative rank by a 0/1 indicator assigns score 0 to all firms failing the persistent-profit screen, dumping them into the extreme short leg rather than excluding or neutralizing them, so the tested portfolio is dominated by the gate itself rather than by conditional accrual information.

It leans on two well-known effects (working-capital accruals and gross profitability), but uses a genuinely distinct data footprint (act/che/lct/dlc, sale−cogs) and a defensible credibility mechanism — margins unaccompanied by working-capital accumulation — that is not a simple restatement of either parent anomaly.

Signed accruals times cash-flow profitability is close to a direct rediscovery of the Sloan accrual anomaly conditioned on operating profitability, and it is nearly redundant with the Accrual-Earnings Durability Product in this same batch (abs vs. signed accruals, oancf vs. ib), so it adds no independent information.

The earnings-vs-cash-flow volatility mismatch as a smoothing detector plus a weakest-link MIN aggregation is the most original construction in the batch and is sign-coherent, but note that accruals are mechanically ib−oancf so the two channels may be highly collinear, which would make the bottleneck structure inert.

This is a cosmetic re-specification of the archived Clean Working-Capital Margin signal (magnitude of working-capital accruals interacted with an earnings-quality/persistence screen) that mainly swaps the margin-stability leg for a profitability-count indicator and RANK for IND_ZSCORE, and the 0/1 multiplier also dumps a large ties-at-zero mass into the middle of the sort.

The construction is internally coherent, but it reuses the archived "low accrual noise × stable margin" weakest-link template with only a line-item substitution, and the tax leg edges into the well-documented tax-expense/book-tax-difference anomalies while relying on sparsely and inconsistently reported txp.

The excess volatility of receivable/inventory adjustments relative to demand volatility is a genuinely distinct construct rather than a repackaged accrual level, though three-period VOL estimates are very noisy, the sign conventions of recch/invch are handled only by absolute value, and the revenue-stability leg overlaps with known earnings-volatility effects.

dpc and dp are near-identical for the vast majority of firms, so the first leg is a mostly-degenerate mass at zero dominated by data idiosyncrasies, leaving the MIN effectively driven by stable asset turnover — a known profitability/DuPont characteristic — inside an already-tested template.

The hypothesis and expression align (cash-efficient internal capital accumulation), but dividing a trend by a small nonnegative accrual denominator makes the ratio highly unstable and likely denominator-dominated even after 1% winsorization, so a scaled difference or double-sort would be a cleaner test of the same idea.

The conjunctive MIN correctly implements the stated "both high leverage and opaque accruals" penalty with a sign that matches the expression's direction, and the financing-pressure × accounting-flexibility interaction is economically distinct from a standalone leverage or accrual effect, with the main risk being coverage of txach/aoloch.

This is the archive's Clean Working-Capital Margin with the only change being the MA/VOL window shortened from 5 to 3 — a purely cosmetic parameter tweak of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantive mechanism change.

Replacing the unstable small-denominator ratio with a rank-space conjunctive MIN is a defensible functional-form repair that is internally consistent (both components are "good" states, so positive sign is correct), though it recycles the same two ingredients as the prior weak signal and is only marginally novel.

This is the archived Leveraged Opaque-Accrual Penalty with MIN flipped to MAX on identical inputs — a single-operator variant whose long leg collapses toward low-leverage, low-accrual firms and therefore largely re-tests the well-known leverage/accrual quality effects rather than a new interaction.

Inventory growth measured against realized throughput is essentially the published Abarbanell–Bushee inventory-versus-sales fundamental signal and the Thomas–Zhang inventory-change anomaly, so the trend-window wrapper does not make it a genuinely new cross-theme mechanism.

Subtracting raw trends of two ratios with wildly different scales (gross margin bounded near [0,1] versus wcap/sale, which is unbounded and sign-unstable) means the composite will be dominated by the working-capital-intensity trend, reducing it to a noisy proxy for the known working-capital-accrual/NOA-growth anomaly rather than the stated margin-versus-capital comparison.

The conjunctive design is internally consistent, the two trend components are commensurably scaled by assets, and requiring debt-financing-adjusted cash confirmation of retained-earnings growth is a substantively different test from the prior MAX-based "corroboration" gap, though it overlaps partly with known external-financing anomalies.

This recombines the exact two ingredients of the archive's generation-0 winner (working-capital accrual magnitude and mean-minus-vol gross margin) into a single ratio, and the ABS() charge penalizes working-capital *releases* — cash-generating events — which contradicts the stated logic of charging for working-capital *investment*.

The sign conventions are handled correctly and the TS_MIN "floor" is a mild twist, but ni+recch+invch scaled by assets is essentially cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016), a well-published anomaly, and it is also a close aggregator variant of the archive's Receivable-Neutral Earnings Durability.

Internally consistent and a genuine structural improvement over the prior discrete sign-count version, though the second leg (|NI − adjusted CF|) is close to a standard absolute-accruals quality measure and apalch/oancf availability will keep coverage thin.

The stated rationale is economically confused — depreciation is a genuine noncash charge, so subtracting dpc from oancf simply walks back toward accrual earnings, making the signal a stable-earnings-margin measure (close to known profitability/earnings-stability anomalies) rather than a test of cash-flow quality.

The threshold-crossing/benchmark-beating mechanism is coherent and the expected negative sign matches the expression, but the 0–5 integer output creates heavy ties and coarse portfolio sorts of the kind that already produced weak results for the archive's discrete count signal, and it overlaps substantially with the classic accruals anomaly.

The MIN bottleneck does not implement the stated conditional hypothesis (the short leg pools low-accrual firms with declining-revenue firms rather than high-accrual/low-growth firms), and the positive expected sign leans on an in-sample sign flip from a prior archive result while embedding a revenue-trend leg whose own return direction is ambiguous.

Net income minus noncash working-capital accruals scaled by assets is essentially cash-based operating profitability (Sloan accruals plus Ball et al. cash profitability), so despite the internally consistent profit gate this is a repackaging of two of the best-known published anomalies rather than a cross-theme discovery.

The depreciation-versus-sales growth congruence construct is not a standard published anomaly and the expansion gate is a substantively motivated response to the archived signal's FMB/alpha sign conflict (matched contractions polluting the long leg), though the prior alpha was reliably negative at t=-1.8 so the gate may reorder rather than repair the spread.

Once the gate is applied the payoff variable is simply the signed receivables accrual scaled by sales, i.e. the receivables component of the Sloan accrual anomaly, and the margin-improvement indicator is too thin an interaction to make it a distinct mechanism.

Δcash minus Δtotal-debt over assets is close to the established net-external-financing/debt-issuance anomaly, and the archive already tested the same cash-net-of-debt confirmation channel (Debt-Adjusted Cash Retention, fmb 0.73, alpha -0.016) with only the gating variable changed here.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Cash-Converted Margin Improvement (same NEG(Δwcap/sale) payoff, gate swapped from margin trend to revenue-productivity trend and MIN swapped for an indicator product), and the underlying payoff is the working-capital accrual anomaly itself, so the prior FMB/alpha sign conflict is unlikely to be diagnosed by this change.

The expression is literally the inner subexpression of the archived Demand-Accrual Volatility Alignment signal, and it is internally inconsistent because VOL(revt/at) is an order of magnitude larger than VOL((|recch|+|invch|)/at), so after NEG the score is dominated by and increasing in revenue volatility — the opposite of the stated stability hypothesis.

This keeps the identical sales-productivity gate from the archived "Expansion-Gated Depreciation Congruence" and swaps one depreciation-policy-consistency measure for a highly correlated one (|Δdpc−Δsale| → VOL(dpc/sale)), which is closer to a cosmetic re-parameterization than a diagnosis of why that signal's alpha was insignificant despite a 4.6 t-stat.

The expression is the archived "Margin Improvement Funding Test" (low current WC accrual, margin-up gate) plus a positively-weighted lagged WC accrual level, which rewards firms that previously accumulated large working-capital accruals — the opposite of the well-documented accrual anomaly — so the "harvesting" story does not match what the formula computes.

The framing is confused (subtracting apalch−recch penalizes payable growth *and* receivable growth, so it is an accrual-quality penalty, not a "cash-conversion adjustment," since rising payables supply cash) and it subtracts a flow level from a first difference with no scale normalization, so the ranked signal will be dominated by a plain net trade-accrual sort already well covered by the published accrual anomaly.

Conditioning on margin deterioration and measuring second-difference instability (rather than the level) of working-capital intensity is a coherent, non-redundant instability test that uses the complementary half of the sample from the archive's margin-improvement gates and correctly avoids rewarding distress-driven liquidation.

This simply bolts together two existing archive components — the TS_MIN(ni/at) profitability floor from "Persistent-Profit Accrual Concentration" and the (oancf−apalch)/at construct from "Supplier-Neutral Cash-Profit Persistence" — recasting the latter's sign count as a 3-period trend, and both parents already showed weak evidence, so the incremental information content is thin and close to a cash-flow-improvement/profitability-trend rediscovery.

This is essentially the third pass at the same construct (gen-1 "Demand-Accrual Volatility Alignment" and gen-4 "Stable-Demand Accrual Noise Screen"), changing only the accrual scaler (at → revt), the demand-stability proxy, and the combination operator back to a MIN bottleneck already tried in gen 1.

The expression is internally consistent with the stated hypothesis and the sign is correct, but it is only the MIN-intersection of two already-archived margin-improvement-conditioned signals, so it is an incremental conjunction (with further coverage loss) rather than a new mechanism.

The disjoint-branch regime switch is a reasonable coverage-expanding idea, but because each branch's IND_ZSCORE is computed over the full cross-section on differently-shaped variables (signed accruals vs. a nonnegative |ACCEL| term), the union will carry a mean level shift between regimes, so the composite risks loading on the margin-improvement dummy itself rather than on working-capital quality.

The refinement is motivated by a specific, correctly-read diagnostic (strong FMB but weak alpha on the expansion-gated congruence signal, implying generic expansion exposure in the tails), and the added |ΔWC|/at bottleneck matches the hypothesis' "little noncash accrual" wording and plausibly attacks the diagnosed problem.

Multiplying a weak archived signal by book leverage grafts a well-known distress/leverage characteristic that FF5 (via HML/CMA) and the prior failed Leveraged Opaque-Accrual Penalty already speak to, and the rank-product form makes it hard to attribute any result to the claimed working-capital-stress mechanism rather than to leverage alone.

This is essentially a sign reversal of the archived Hidden Trade-Credit Churn signal rationalized after the fact by its negative alpha, and the swapped gate does not supply an independent ex-ante reason why gross offsetting AR/AP churn should be *rewarded*, so it reads as fitting to a prior backtest sign.

The core term (ni−oancf)/at − Δwcap/at is mechanically dominated by depreciation and amortization, so penalizing its absolute value is largely a low-capital-intensity screen rather than an opacity screen, which makes the hypothesis inconsistent with what the expression computes and makes the depreciation-mismatch gate partly redundant with the signal itself.

The hypothesis is verbatim identical to the archived "Two-Sided Margin Accounting Confirmation" and the only change is swapping the nested MIN for SUMRANK plus ZSCORE for IND_ZSCORE — a legitimate coverage repair of a signal that never evaluated, but still an aggregation-operator variant of an existing proposal rather than a new mechanism.

Sign-consistent and internally coherent (both terms are NEG(ABS(.)) stability measures under a genuine margin-decline gate), but it is essentially a rank-sum of two already-tested archive signals whose individual evidence was weak in both FMB and alpha, so the expected marginal information is limited.

The add-back of DELTA(wcap) to oancf is economically correct and the weakest-link MAX construction is well-formed, but the signal is ultimately a dual fundamental-volatility score and therefore sits close to the known earnings-volatility/smoothness anomaly, so incremental content over that literature is the main risk.

The first leg is the exact margin-persistence term from the generation-0 "Clean Working-Capital Margin," and replacing ABS(working-capital accrual level) with VOL(working-capital accrual) and MUL with MIN is a near-substitute recombination of that same signal rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Directionally consistent and a genuine congruence test, though the two margins are not truly commensurate (gross margin excludes SG&A/tax while the cash margin does not), so divergence will partly reflect operating-expense dynamics rather than accounting corroboration, and the symmetric ABS penalizes favorable cash outperformance as well.

This is the archived "Dual Margin Cash Confirmation" with (oancf - apalch) replaced by (oancf + DELTA(wcap)) and no other change, i.e., a cosmetic input substitution on a construct that already produced a weak FMB slope and a negative FF5 alpha.

This is the archived "Asset-Release Margin Funding Quality" with IND_ZSCORE swapped for ZSCORE(IND_RANK) — a purely cosmetic robustification that the objective explicitly discourages as a response to FMB/alpha sign disagreement, and rank-bounding alone will not explain why the long-short alpha was reliably negative (t = -2.38) while the slope was strongly positive.

Switching MIN to MAX in the archived "Margin-Decline Working-Capital Squeeze" is a mechanical aggregation tweak on an identical variable set and gate, and it offers no diagnosis of that signal's contradictory negative alpha (t = -2.15) despite a positive slope.

Internally consistent and a legitimate isolation of the depreciation-recognition channel from the archived "Depreciation-Supported Margin Improvement" (replacing the margin rank with a clean gate), though it is a thin single-variable signal whose economics compete with the well-known negative asset-growth/capital-intensity effect embedded in a rising dpc/sale trend.

Sign-consistent but gratuitously double-negated (NEG(trend) with a negative expected sign is just the trend with a positive sign), and it exhausts the same single variable as proposal #3 on the complementary gate while overlapping heavily with the archived "Margin-Decline Depreciation Stability."

The acceleration-based gate is an economically distinct conditioning variable (operating inflection rather than level improvement) and the expression matches the stated sign, but it is the third gate variant applied to the already-tested |ACCEL(wcap/sale)| core, so the incremental information content is modest.

Internally coherent and the cleanest decomposition in this batch (liability-side accrual channel conditioned on a durable-margin gate), but the reviewer should note that penalizing nondebt current-liability growth runs opposite to the sign implied for operating-liability accruals in the standard Sloan accrual anomaly, so the mechanism needs to survive an accruals control.

This is the archived gen-8 "Smooth-Earnings Cash-to-Accrual Substitution" signal with one extra profitability indicator bolted on — a cosmetic sample filter rather than a new mechanism, and it will mostly trim coverage of an already-narrow qualifying set.

Internally consistent and the persistence idea is defensible, but three-period smoothing of both legs of the identical archived winner is a standard time-averaging tweak, not a substantively different construct.

Replacing the two-flow conjunction with a stock-composition drift measure is a genuinely different construction of the mechanism with better continuity and coverage, though reviewers should watch that it does not collapse into a mechanical change-in-cash / asset-growth proxy.

Swapping the earnings-smoothness gate for the durable-margin gate is economically coherent and the sign logic is correct, but it is a conditioning-variable substitution on an existing winner rather than a new economic channel, and the hard indicator gate again discards continuous information.

Another gate swap on the same substitution score, and the margin-improvement indicator combined with a working-capital funding score is very close to the already-archived "Margin Improvement Funding Test," so incremental information content is likely small.

This is a linear blend of two archived signals whose components share the same dominant term (DELTA(act) − DELTA(che)), so it double-counts a single accrual channel and functions as an ensemble rather than a testable new hypothesis.
